metadata.description: Claim Adjustment Reason Codes (CARC) with explanations

carc_codes.detailed_explanation: The deductible amount is the portion of the allowed amount that the patient is responsible for paying before insurance coverage begins. This is not a denial but rather a patient responsibility adjustment.
common_causes: Patient has not met annual deductible

recommended_actions.details: Send patient statement for the deductible portion
Check if patient has met deductible with other claims

carc_codes.detailed_explanation: The coinsurance amount represents the patient's share of the allowed amount after the deductible has been met. This is typically a percentage of the allowed amount.

recommended_actions.details: Send patient statement for coinsurance amount
Confirm correct coinsurance rate was applied

carc_codes.detailed_explanation: The procedure code submitted is not consistent with the modifier used, or a required modifier is missing. Modifiers provide additional information about the service performed.
common_causes: Modifier not applicable to the CPT code

recommended_actions.details: Check LCD/NCD for required modifiers
Add or correct modifier and resubmit claim
If modifier was correct, submit appeal with documentation

carc_codes.short_description: Claim lacks information needed for adjudication
carc_codes.detailed_explanation: The claim is missing information that is required for the payer to process and adjudicate the claim. This could include patient demographics, provider information, or clinical details.

recommended_actions.details: Check all required fields are populated
Contact patient or referring provider for missing data
Submit claim with all required information

carc_codes.detailed_explanation: An exact duplicate claim or service line was already processed. The payer has already adjudicated this claim and will not pay twice for the same service.
common_causes: Electronic and paper claim both submitted

recommended_actions.details: Verify if original claim was paid
Check for duplicate submissions in billing system
If services were distinct, appeal with documentation

carc_codes.short_description: Time limit for filing has expired
carc_codes.detailed_explanation: The claim was not submitted within the payer's timely filing deadline. Most payers require claims to be submitted within 90-365 days from the date of service.

recommended_actions.details: Check payer-specific timely filing requirements
Submit appeal with proof of timely filing or valid reason for delay

recommended_actions.action: Write off if deadline truly missed
recommended_actions.details: Adjust claim if no valid appeal basis exists

carc_codes.detailed_explanation: The service is not covered under the patient's benefit plan. This may be due to plan exclusions, service limitations, or the service not being a covered benefit.

recommended_actions.details: Check patient's benefit plan for covered services
Ensure documentation supports medical necessity
If ABN was obtained, bill patient for non-covered service

carc_codes.detailed_explanation: The charge is not covered because it exceeds the fee schedule, maximum allowable, or contracted rate. The difference between billed and allowed amounts is not payable.

recommended_actions.details: Verify allowed amount for the service
Write off amount exceeding allowed amount
Bill patient for non-covered portion if permitted

carc_codes.detailed_explanation: The service was not authorized by the payer. Prior authorization was required but not obtained, or the authorization was invalid or expired.
common_causes: Service performed differs from authorized service

recommended_actions.details: Check if authorization was obtained and valid
Some payers allow retro-auth for emergent services
Submit appeal demonstrating medical necessity

carc_codes.detailed_explanation: The required precertification or prior authorization was not obtained before the service was rendered. The payer requires advance approval for this service.

recommended_actions.details: Verify if service requires prior auth
Submit retro-auth request if allowed by payer
Demonstrate medical necessity and urgency
